label: prop:s4-s3-half-symmetric-projection
title: $S_3$-trivial share of the half-symmetric part of $H_4$ under $S_4 \downarrow S_3$ branching
html:
In the half-symmetric part of H_4(q) at q = 1 (one irreducible from each conjugate pair \{(4),(1^4)\} and \{(3,1),(2,1,1)\}, plus half of the self-conjugate (2,2)), the weighted dimension is 5 and the weighted multiplicity of the trivial S_3-representation under S_4 \downarrow S_3 is 2. The S_3-trivial share of the half-symmetric part is therefore 2/5.

This is a statement about branching multiplicities only. It does not identify a cell of a hyperbolic decomposition. The complement S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 of the Borromean rings is the union of two regular ideal octahedra [adams1985hyperbolic], so \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 2V_{\mathrm{oct}} = 8G, where V_{\mathrm{oct}} = 4G \approx 3.6639 and G is Catalan's constant. There is no eight-cell octahedral decomposition for the ratio 2/5 to select from.
